nodes.description: CBT-AR combines regular eating, nutritional planning, presentation-specific exposure and relapse prevention. nodes.description: Low interest in eating, low hunger and early satiation can limit intake. Within the lack-of-interest phenotype group, greater symptom severity correlated with lower right hypothalamus activation during a fasting visual-food-cue task. The group did not show lower hypothalamus activation than healthy controls overall. This cross-sectional association does not establish hypothalamic dysfunction as the cause of restriction or identify the responsible endocrine cell type. In a separate self-report study, ARFID severity correlated with lower anticipatory pleasure even after food items were removed. This broader reward association and the contribution of depressive symptoms do not establish a food-specific reward defect or its causal direction.

nodes.description: A Swedish twin study estimated substantial genetic liability for a broad childhood ARFID phenotype defined from parent reports and health registers. Its best-fitting model estimated heritability of 0.79 (95% CI 0.70-0.85) and a nonshared environmental contribution of 0.21 (95% CI 0.15-0.30). Ascertainment emphasized sensory restriction, did not directly assess every diagnostic exclusion, and included a sibling-contrast parameter. These estimates do not identify causal genes or establish equal heritability across ages and ARFID presentations. Common-variant studies also support genetic contributions to avoidant/restrictive eating, but use different ascertainment: ARFI traits in a Norwegian population cohort and an algorithm-derived risk score in an autism cohort. Neither establishes a single causal pathway or a diagnostic genetic test for ARFID.

nodes.description: The convergent core behavior: persistent avoidance or restriction of food intake reached by any of the three drivers, critically without the drive for thinness, fear of weight gain, or body-image disturbance that defines anorexia nervosa. This absence of weight/shape motivation is the defining contrast with anorexia nervosa. The three drivers are dimensional and frequently co-occur rather than being mutually exclusive subtypes: an empirical latent-class analysis of 319 children/adolescents found a mixed (combined) presentation to be the single most common class.
